bookInfo.name: New History of the Five Dynasties

title.zh: 卷三十五 唐六臣傳第二十三: 張文蔚 楊涉 張策 趙光逢 薛貽矩 蘇循
title.en: Volume 35 Biographies 15: Zhan Wenyu, Yang She, Zhang Ce, Zhao Guangfeng, Xue Yiju, Su Xun
title.raw: 卷三十五 唐六臣傳第二十三: 張文蔚 楊涉 張策 趙光逢 薛貽矩 蘇循 Volume 35 Biographies 15: Zhan Wenyu, Yang She, Zhang Ce, Zhao Guangfeng, Xue Yiju, Su Xun

sentences.zh: 甚哉，白馬之禍，悲夫，可為流涕者矣！

translations.literal: How extreme—the calamity of White Horse! Alas, a matter that could draw tears!
translations.idiomatic: How extreme—the White Horse massacre! Alas—it could draw tears!

sentences.zh: 然士之生死，豈其一身之事哉？

translations.literal: Yet is a gentleman’s life and death merely his own affair?
translations.idiomatic: Yet is a gentleman’s life and death only his own affair?

sentences.zh: 初，唐天祐三年，梁王欲以嬖吏張廷範為太常卿，唐宰相裴樞以謂太常卿唐常以清流為之，廷範乃梁客將，不可。

translations.literal: At first, in the third year of Tianyou of Tang, the Prince of Liang wished to make his favorite clerk Zhang Tingfan Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; Tang’s chief minister Pei Shu held that the Grand Master of Splendid Happiness was by Tang custom always drawn from the pure stream, while Tingfan was a Liang guest-general—unacceptable.
translations.idiomatic: In Tang’s third Tianyou year the Prince of Liang wanted his favorite Zhang Tingfan as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; Chief Minister Pei Shu said that post belonged to the pure stream, not a Liang guest-general.

sentences.zh: 梁王由此大怒，曰：「吾常語裴樞純厚不陷浮薄，今亦為此邪！

translations.literal: The Prince of Liang thereupon raged greatly and said, “I always said Pei Shu was pure and thick and would not sink into shallowness—yet now he does this too!
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Liang raged: “I called Pei Shu pure and solid—yet now he does this too!

sentences.zh: 」是歲四月，彗出西北，掃文昌、軒轅、天市，宰相柳璨希梁王旨，歸其譴於大臣，於是左僕射裴樞、獨孤損、右僕射崔遠、守太保致仕趙崇、兵部侍郎王贊、工部尚書王溥、吏部尚書陸扆皆以無罪貶，同日賜死於白馬驛。

translations.literal: That year in the fourth month a comet appeared in the northwest, sweeping Wenchang, Xuanyuan, and the Celestial Market; Chief Minister Liu Can, hoping to please the Prince of Liang, laid the omen’s blame on the great ministers; thereupon Left Vice Director Pei Shu, Dugu Sun, Right Vice Director Cui Yuan, Retired Grand Preceptor Zhao Chong, Vice Minister of War Wang Zan, Minister of Works Wang Pu, and Minister of Personnel Lu Yi were all demoted without crime and on the same day ordered to die at White Horse Station.
translations.idiomatic: That fourth month a comet swept the northwest heavens; Liu Can pleased Liang by blaming the ministers; Pei Shu, Dugu Sun, Cui Yuan, Zhao Chong, Wang Zan, Wang Pu, and Lu Yi were demoted without crime and executed the same day at White Horse Station.

sentences.zh: 凡搢紳之士與唐而不與梁者，皆誣以朋黨，坐貶死者數百人，而朝廷為之一空。

translations.literal: Every gentry scholar who sided with Tang and not Liang was charged with faction, punished and killed by the hundreds, and the court was emptied at a stroke.
translations.idiomatic: Every scholar who sided with Tang, not Liang, was charged with faction; hundreds died—and the court stood empty.

sentences.zh: 明年三月，唐哀帝遜位於梁，遣中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事張文蔚為冊禮使，禮部尚書蘇循為副；

translations.literal: In the third month of the next year Emperor Ai of Tang abdicated to Liang, sending Vice Director of the Secretariat and Concurrent Palace Attendant Zhang Wenwei as commissioner of investiture rites, with Minister of Rites Su Xun as deputy;
translations.idiomatic: Next year’s third month, Emperor Ai abdicated to Liang, sending Zhang Wenwei as investiture commissioner and Su Xun as deputy;

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事楊涉為押傳國寶使，翰林學士、中書舍人張策為副；

translations.literal: Vice Director Yang She as commissioner escorting the imperial seal and treasures, with Hanlin Academician and Secretariat Drafter Zhang Ce as deputy;
translations.idiomatic: Yang She escorting the imperial seal, Zhang Ce deputy;

sentences.zh: 御史大夫薛貽矩為押金寶使，尚書左丞趙光逢為副。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Xue Yiju as commissioner escorting the gold treasures, with Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Zhao Guangfeng as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Yiju escorting the gold treasures, Zhao Guangfeng deputy.

sentences.zh: 四月甲子，文蔚等自上源驛奉冊寶，乘輅車，導以金吾仗衛、太常鹵簿，朝梁於金祥殿。

translations.literal: On jiazi of the fourth month Wenwei and the rest brought the register and treasures from Shangyuan Post, rode the imperial carriage, were led by the Golden Guard and Grand Musician’s procession, and attended upon Liang at Jinxiang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi of the fourth month they brought register and treasures from Shangyuan Post in the imperial carriage, with Golden Guard and ritual escort, to attend Liang at Jinxiang Hall.

sentences.zh: 王袞冕南面，臣文蔚、臣循奉冊升殿，進讀已，臣涉、臣策奉傳國璽，臣貽矩、臣光逢奉金寶，以次升，進讀已，降，率文武百官北面舞蹈再拜賀。

translations.literal: The king in full regalia faced south; ministers Wenwei and Xun bore the register up the hall and read it; ministers She and Ce bore the transmission seal; ministers Yiju and Guangfeng bore the gold treasures; each in turn ascended and read; then descended and led civil and military officials in facing north, dancing and bowing twice in congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: The king faced south in full regalia; Wenwei and Xun read the register; She and Ce bore the transmission seal; Yiju and Guangfeng bore the gold treasures; then all civil and military officials faced north, danced, and bowed twice in congratulation.

sentences.zh: 夫一太常卿與社稷孰為重？

translations.literal: Which weighs more—one Grand Master of Splendid Happiness or the altars of state?
translations.idiomatic: Which matters more—one Grand Master of Splendid Happiness or the realm itself?

sentences.zh: 使樞等不死，尚惜一卿，其肯以國與人乎？

translations.literal: Had Shu and the rest not died, they would still have grudged one minister’s post—would they have been willing to give the state to another?
translations.idiomatic: Had Shu and the rest lived, they would have fought over one post—would they have surrendered the realm?

sentences.zh: 雖樞等之力未必能存唐，然必不亡唐而獨存也。

translations.literal: Though Shu and the rest’s strength might not have preserved Tang, they would never have let Tang perish while they alone survived.
translations.idiomatic: They might not have saved Tang—but they would never have let Tang fall while they alone survived.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 唐之亡也，賢人君子既與之共盡，其餘在者皆庸懦不肖、傾險獪猾、趨利賣國之徒也。

translations.literal: When Tang perished, worthy men and gentlemen had already died with it; those who remained were mediocre, cowardly, unworthy, treacherous, crafty, profit-seeking sellers of the state.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang fell, the worthy had already died with it; what remained were cowards, traitors, and men who sold the state for gain.

sentences.zh: 不然，安能蒙恥忍辱於梁庭如此哉！

translations.literal: Otherwise how could they have borne such shame and humiliation in Liang’s court!
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise how could they have borne such shame in Liang’s court!

sentences.zh: 作《唐六臣傳》。

translations.literal: I composed the “Biographies of the Six Tang Ministers.”
translations.idiomatic: Hence I wrote the “Biographies of the Six Tang Ministers.”

sentences.zh: 張文蔚

translations.literal: Zhang Wenwei
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wenwei

sentences.zh: 張文蔚，字右華，河間人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Wenwei, courtesy name Youhua, was a man of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wenwei, courtesy name Youhua, was from Hejian.

sentences.zh: 初以文行知名，舉進士及第。

translations.literal: At first he was known for literary conduct and passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He was known for learning and passed the jinshi.

sentences.zh: 唐昭宗時，為翰林學士承旨。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Zhaozong of Tang he was Hanlin Academician in charge.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhaozong he was chief Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 是時，天子微弱，制度已隳，文蔚居翰林，制詔四方，獨守大體。

translations.literal: At that time the Son of Heaven was weak and institutions already broken; Wenwei in the Hanlin drafted edicts for all quarters yet alone kept to the great pattern.
translations.idiomatic: The throne was weak and institutions broken; in the Hanlin, Wenwei drafted edicts for the realm yet held to the great pattern.

sentences.zh: 昭宗遷洛，拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: When Zhaozong moved to Luoyang, Wenwei was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Concurrent Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaozong moved to Luoyang, Wenwei became Vice Director and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 柳璨殺裴樞等七人，蔓引朝士，輒加誅殺，縉紳相視以目，皆不自保，文蔚力講解之，朝士多賴以全活。

translations.literal: When Liu Can killed Pei Shu and six others, he extended the net to courtiers and added executions at will; gentry exchanged glances and none felt safe; Wenwei argued forcefully for their release, and many courtiers owed their lives to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Can killed Pei Shu and six others and hunted courtiers, gentry exchanged fearful glances; Wenwei argued for mercy, and many owed him their lives.

sentences.zh: 梁太祖立，仍以文蔚為相，梁初制度皆文蔚所裁定。

translations.literal: When Taizu of Liang took the throne, Wenwei was still made chief minister; Liang’s early institutions were all set by Wenwei.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang’s Taizu took the throne, Wenwei remained chief minister; Liang’s early institutions were his work.

sentences.zh: 文蔚居家亦孝悌。

translations.literal: At home too Wenwei was filial and brotherly.
translations.idiomatic: At home he was filial and brotherly.

sentences.zh: 開平二年，太祖北巡，留文蔚西都，以暴疾卒，贈右僕射。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiping, Taizu toured the north and left Wenwei in the western capital; he died suddenly of acute illness and was posthumously made Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiping’s second year Taizu toured north and left Wenwei in the western capital; he died suddenly and was posthumously made Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 楊涉，祖收，唐懿宗時宰相；

translations.literal: Yang She—his grandfather Shou was chief minister under Emperor Yizong of Tang;
translations.idiomatic: Yang She’s grandfather Shou was chief minister under Yizong;

sentences.zh: 父嚴，官至兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: his father Yan rose to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: his father Yan rose to Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 涉舉進士，昭宗時為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: She passed the jinshi and under Zhaozong was Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: She passed the jinshi and under Zhaozong was Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 哀帝即位，拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ai took the throne, She was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Concurrent Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ai took the throne, She became Vice Director and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 涉，唐名家，世守禮法，而性特謹厚，不幸遭唐之亂，拜相之日，與家人相對泣下，顧謂其子凝式曰：「吾不能脫此網羅，禍將至矣，必累爾等。

translations.literal: She was of a famous Tang house, generations guarding ritual law, and by nature especially cautious and thick; unluckily he met Tang’s disorder; on the day he became chief minister he wept facing his family and, turning to his son Ningshi, said, “I cannot escape this net; disaster is coming and will surely involve you all.
translations.idiomatic: Of a famous Tang house, ritual-bound and deeply cautious, he met the dynasty’s fall; on the day he became chief minister he wept with his family and told his son Ningshi, “I cannot escape this net—disaster will come and drag you down.

sentences.zh: 」唐亡，事梁為門下侍郎、同中書門下平章事，在位三年，俯首無所施為，罷為左僕射，知貢舉，後數年卒。

translations.literal: When Tang perished he served Liang as Vice Director of the Chancellery and Concurrent Palace Attendant; in office three years he bowed his head and accomplished nothing, was dismissed as Left Vice Director, supervised the examinations, and died some years later.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang fell he served Liang as chief minister three years, head bowed, accomplishing nothing; he was dismissed to Left Vice Director, supervised examinations, and died years later.

sentences.zh: 子凝式，有文詞，善筆劄，歷事梁、唐、晉、漢、周，常以心疾致仕，居於洛陽，官至太子太保。

translations.literal: His son Ningshi had literary talent and skill at letters; he served Liang, Tang, Jin, Han, and Zhou, often retired for heart trouble, lived in Luoyang, and rose to Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ningshi was literate and skilled in letters; he served five dynasties, often retired for heart trouble, lived in Luoyang, and rose to Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: ○張策

translations.literal: ○ Zhang Ce
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ce

sentences.zh: 張策，字少逸，河西敦煌人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Ce, courtesy name Shaoyi, was a man of Dunhuang in Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ce, courtesy name Shaoyi, was from Dunhuang in Hexi.

sentences.zh: 父同，為唐容管經略使。

translations.literal: His father Tong was Tang’s military commissioner of Rongguan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tong was Tang’s commissioner of Rongguan.

sentences.zh: 策少聰悟好學，通章句。

translations.literal: Ce in youth was clever, fond of study, and versed in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Ce was clever, fond of study, and versed in the classics.

sentences.zh: 父同，居洛陽敦化裏，浚井得古鼎，銘曰：「魏黃初元年春二月，匠吉千。

translations.literal: His father Tong, dwelling in Dunhua Lane in Luoyang, dredged a well and found an ancient tripod; the inscription read: “In spring, second month, first year of Huangchu of Wei, craftsman Ji Qian.”
translations.idiomatic: His father Tong, in Dunhua Lane, Luoyang, dredged a well and found an ancient tripod inscribed: “Spring, second month, first year of Huangchu of Wei, craftsman Ji Qian.”

sentences.zh: 」同以為奇，策時年十三，居同側，啟曰：「漢建安二十五年，曹公薨，改元延康。

translations.literal: Tong thought it marvelous; Ce was then thirteen, at Tong’s side, and said: “In the twenty-fifth year of Jian’an of Han, Lord Cao died and the era name was changed to Yankang.
translations.idiomatic: Tong thought it marvelous; Ce, thirteen, at his side said, “In Han’s twenty-fifth Jian’an year Lord Cao died and the era became Yankang.

sentences.zh: 是歲十月，文帝受禪，又改黃初，是黃初元年無二月也，銘何謬邪？

translations.literal: That year in the tenth month Emperor Wen received the abdication and again changed to Huangchu—so in the first year of Huangchu there was no second month; how is the inscription wrong?”
translations.idiomatic: That tenth month Wen accepted the throne and changed to Huangchu—so Huangchu’s first year had no second month. How is the inscription wrong?”

sentences.zh: 」同大驚異之。

translations.literal: Tong was greatly startled and marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: Tong was astonished.

sentences.zh: 策少好浮圖之說，乃落發為僧，居長安慈恩寺。

translations.literal: Ce in youth loved Buddhist teaching, shaved his head, and became a monk at Cien Temple in Chang’an.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he loved Buddhism, shaved his head, and became a monk at Cien Temple in Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 黃巢犯長安，策乃返初服，奉父母以避亂，居田里十餘年。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao attacked Chang’an, Ce returned to lay dress, supported his parents to flee disorder, and dwelt in the countryside more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao took Chang’an, Ce returned to lay dress, led his parents into hiding, and lived in the countryside ten years.

sentences.zh: 召拜廣文館博士。

translations.literal: He was summoned and made Doctor of the Broad Learning Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Doctor of the Broad Learning Hall.

sentences.zh: 邠州王行瑜辟觀察支使。

translations.literal: Wang Xingyu of Binzhou took him as administrative aide to the observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xingyu of Binzhou made him observation administrative aide.

sentences.zh: 晉王李克用攻行瑜，策與婢肩輿其母東歸，行積雪中，行者憐之。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jin Li Keyong attacked Xingyu, Ce with a maid shouldered a sedan for his mother and went east; traveling through piled snow, passersby pitied them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Jin attacked Xingyu, Ce had a maid carry his mother east through deep snow; passersby pitied them.

sentences.zh: 梁太祖兼四鎮，辟鄭、滑支使，以母喪解職。

translations.literal: Taizu of Liang held four commands and took Ce as administrative aide to Zheng and Hua; he left office for his mother’s mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Liang’s Taizu held four commands and made him aide at Zheng and Hua; he left for his mother’s mourning.

sentences.zh: 服除，入唐為膳部員外郎。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he entered Tang as Vice Director of the Board of Food.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he entered Tang as Vice Director of the Board of Food.

sentences.zh: 華州韓建辟判官，建徙許州，以為掌書記，建遣策聘於太祖，太祖見而喜曰：「張夫子至矣。

translations.literal: Han Jian of Huazhou took him as administrative judge; when Jian moved to Xuzhou he made Ce chief secretary; Jian sent Ce as envoy to Taizu; Taizu saw him and rejoiced: “Master Zhang has come.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jian of Huazhou made him judge; when Jian moved to Xuzhou he made Ce chief secretary and sent him to Taizu; Taizu rejoiced: “Master Zhang has come.

sentences.zh: 」遂留以為掌書記，薦之於朝，累拜中書舍人、翰林學士。

translations.literal: He was kept as chief secretary, recommended to court, and rose step by step to Secretariat Drafter and Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu kept him as chief secretary, recommended him to court, and he rose to Secretariat Drafter and Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，遷工部侍郎奉旨。

translations.literal: When Taizu took the throne, Ce was moved to Vice Minister of Works with imperial commission.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took the throne, Ce became Vice Minister of Works with imperial commission.

sentences.zh: 開平二年，拜刑部侍郎、同中書門下平章事，遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiping he was made Vice Minister of Justice and Concurrent Palace Attendant, then Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiping’s second year he became Vice Minister of Justice and Palace Attendant, then Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 以風恙罷為刑部尚書，致仕，卒於洛陽。

translations.literal: For wind ailment he was dismissed to Minister of Justice, retired, and died in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ill with wind ailment, he retired as Minister of Justice and died in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 趙光逢

translations.literal: Zhao Guangfeng
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Guangfeng

sentences.zh: 薛貽矩

translations.literal: Xue Yiju
translations.idiomatic: Xue Yiju

sentences.zh: 薛貽矩，字熙用，河東聞喜人也，仕唐為兵部侍郎、翰林學士承旨。

translations.literal: Xue Yiju, courtesy name Xiyong, was a man of Wenxi in Hedong; he served Tang as Vice Minister of War and Hanlin Academician in charge.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Yiju, courtesy name Xiyong, was from Wenxi in Hedong; he served Tang as Vice Minister of War and chief Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 昭宗自岐還長安，大誅宦者，貽矩時為中尉韓全誨等作畫像贊，坐左遷。

translations.literal: When Zhaozong returned from Qi to Chang’an and executed the eunuchs in great numbers, Yiju had written portrait eulogies for the commandants Han Quanhui and others and was demoted for it.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaozong returned from Qi to Chang’an and slaughtered eunuchs, Yiju had written eulogies for Han Quanhui and others and was demoted.

sentences.zh: 貽矩乃自結於梁太祖，太祖言之於朝，拜吏部尚書，遷御史大夫。

translations.literal: Yiju then attached himself to Taizu of Liang; Taizu spoke for him at court; he was made Minister of Personnel and moved to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He then attached himself to Liang’s Taizu, who spoke for him at court; he became Minister of Personnel, then Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 天祐三年，太祖自長蘆還軍，哀帝遣貽矩來勞，貽矩以臣禮見，太祖揖之升階，貽矩曰：「殿下功德及人，三靈改卜，皇帝方行舜、禹之事，臣安敢違？

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianyou, Taizu returned his army from Changlu; Emperor Ai sent Yiju to comfort the troops; Yiju met him with minister’s rites; Taizu bowed him up the steps; Yiju said, “Your Highness’s merit reaches the people; the three spirits have changed their divination; the emperor is about to do what Shun and Yu did—how dare your servant disobey?”
translations.idiomatic: In Tianyou’s third year Taizu returned from Changlu; Emperor Ai sent Yiju to comfort the army; Yiju used minister’s rites; Taizu bowed him up the steps; Yiju said, “Your merit reaches the people; Heaven has turned; the emperor will do as Shun and Yu—how dare I disobey?”

sentences.zh: 」乃稱臣拜舞，太祖側身以避之。

translations.literal: He then styled himself minister, bowed and danced; Taizu turned aside to avoid it.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed as minister and danced; Taizu turned aside.

sentences.zh: 貽矩還，遂趣哀帝遜位。

translations.literal: When Yiju returned, he pressed Emperor Ai to abdicate.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he pressed Emperor Ai to abdicate.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，拜貽矩中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事，累拜司空。

translations.literal: When Taizu took the throne, Yiju was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Concurrent Palace Attendant, and rose to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took the throne, Yiju became Vice Director and Palace Attendant and rose to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 貽矩為梁相五年，卒，贈侍中。

translations.literal: Yiju was Liang chief minister five years, died, and was posthumously made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was Liang chief minister five years, died, and was posthumously made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 蘇循

translations.literal: Su Xun
translations.idiomatic: Su Xun

sentences.zh: （杜曉附）〉

translations.literal: (Du Xiao appended)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Du Xiao appended)〉

sentences.zh: 蘇循，不知何許人也。

translations.literal: Su Xun—his origin is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Su Xun’s origin is unknown.

sentences.zh: 為人巧佞，阿諛無廉恥，惟利是趨。

translations.literal: As a man he was crafty and fawning, without shame, rushing only toward profit.
translations.idiomatic: He was crafty, fawning, shameless, and rushed only toward profit.

sentences.zh: 事唐為禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He served Tang as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He served Tang as Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 是時，梁太祖已弒昭宗，立哀帝，唐之舊臣皆憤惋切齒，或俯首畏禍，或去不仕，而循特附會梁以希進用。

translations.literal: At that time Taizu of Liang had already murdered Zhaozong and set up Emperor Ai; Tang’s old ministers all gnashed teeth in rage, or bowed their heads fearing disaster, or left and would not serve—yet Xun alone attached himself to Liang hoping for advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu had murdered Zhaozong and enthroned Emperor Ai; Tang’s old ministers gnashed teeth, fled, or bowed in fear—yet Xun alone clung to Liang for advancement.

sentences.zh: 梁兵攻楊行密，大敗於珝河，太祖躁忿，急於禪代，欲邀唐九錫，群臣莫敢當其議，獨循倡言：「梁王功德，天命所歸，宜即受禪。

translations.literal: Liang’s army attacked Yang Xingmi and was routed at Yu River; Taizu was irritable and eager for the abdication, wishing to demand Tang’s Nine Bestowments; no minister dared meet the debate—only Xun proclaimed: “The Prince of Liang’s merit—Heaven’s mandate is his; he should at once receive the abdication.”
translations.idiomatic: Liang attacked Yang Xingmi and was routed at Yu River; Taizu, irritable, sought abdication and the Nine Bestowments; none dared speak—only Xun said, “Heaven’s mandate is Liang’s; take the throne at once.”

sentences.zh: 」明年，梁太祖即位，循為冊禮副使。

translations.literal: The next year Taizu of Liang took the throne; Xun was deputy investiture commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Next year Taizu took the throne; Xun was deputy investiture commissioner.

sentences.zh: 循有子楷，乾寧中舉進士及第，昭宗遣學士陸扆覆落之，楷常慚恨。

translations.literal: Xun had a son Kai who in the Qianning era passed the jinshi; Zhaozong sent Academician Lu Yi to review and strike him from the list; Kai always bore shame and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kai passed the jinshi in the Qianning era; Zhaozong had Lu Yi strike him from the list; Kai bore lasting resentment.

sentences.zh: 及昭宗遇弒，唐政出於梁，楷為起居郎，與柳璨、張廷範等相結，因謂廷範曰：「夫謚者，所以易名而貴信也。

translations.literal: When Zhaozong was murdered and Tang government came from Liang, Kai was Diarist and joined Liu Can, Zhang Tingfan, and others; he told Tingfan: “A posthumous title is meant to change the name and honor truth.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaozong was murdered and Liang held Tang’s government, Kai was Diarist and joined Liu Can and Zhang Tingfan; he told Tingfan, “A posthumous title should honor truth.

sentences.zh: 前有司謚先帝曰『昭』，名實不稱，公為太常卿，予史官也，不可以不言。

translations.literal: The former office gave the late emperor the title “Zhao,” which does not match name and reality; you are Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and I am the historiographer—we cannot stay silent.”
translations.idiomatic: They titled the late emperor “Zhao,” which does not fit; you are Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and I am historiographer—we cannot stay silent.”

sentences.zh: 」乃上疏駁議。

translations.literal: He then memorialized to dispute it.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to dispute it.

sentences.zh: 而廷範本梁客將，嘗求太常卿不得者，廷範亦以此怨唐，因下楷疏廷範，廷範議曰：「臣聞執事堅固之謂恭，亂而不損之謂靈，武而不遂之謂莊，在國逢難之謂閔，因事有功之謂襄，請改謚昭宗皇帝曰恭靈莊閔皇帝，廟號襄宗。」

translations.literal: Tingfan had originally been a Liang guest-general who once sought the Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and failed; he too resented Tang for this; he received Kai’s memorial and proposed: “Your servant has heard that steadfast in conduct is called Gong, undamaged in disorder Ling, martial yet not completed Zhuang, meeting national hardship Min, merit through events Xiang—I beg the posthumous title of Emperor Zhaozong be changed to Emperor Gong-Ling-Zhuang-Min, temple name Xiangzong.”
translations.idiomatic: Tingfan, a Liang guest-general who had failed to win that post, resented Tang; he received Kai’s memorial and proposed insulting posthumous titles—Gong, Ling, Zhuang, Min—and temple name Xiangzong.

sentences.zh: 梁太祖已即位，置酒玄德殿，顧群臣自陳德薄不足以當天命，皆諸公推戴之力。

translations.literal: Taizu of Liang had already taken the throne; he set wine in Xuande Hall and told the assembled ministers his virtue was thin and insufficient for Heaven’s mandate—it was all their pushing and elevation.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu had taken the throne; at Xuande Hall he told ministers his virtue was thin and the throne was their doing.

sentences.zh: 唐之舊臣楊涉、張文蔚等皆慚懼俯伏不能對，獨循與張祎、薛貽矩盛稱梁王功德，所以順天應人者。

translations.literal: Tang’s old ministers Yang She, Zhang Wenwei, and others were all ashamed and fearful, bowed prostrate and could not answer; only Xun with Zhang Yi and Xue Yiju lavishly praised the Prince of Liang’s merit and how he accorded with Heaven and answered men.
translations.idiomatic: Tang’s old ministers Yang She and Zhang Wenwei bowed in shame and could not answer; only Xun, Zhang Yi, and Xue Yiju praised Liang’s merit and Heaven’s mandate.

sentences.zh: 循父子皆自以附會梁得所托，旦夕引首，希見進用，敬翔尤惡之，謂太祖曰：「梁室新造，宜得端士以厚風俗，循父子皆無行，不可立於新朝。

translations.literal: Father and son both thought that by attaching to Liang they had found patronage, craned their necks morning and evening hoping for employment; Jing Xiang especially hated them and told Taizu: “The Liang house is newly made; it should have upright men to thicken custom; father and son Xun are both without conduct and cannot stand in the new court.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son thought Liang was their patron and craned their necks for office; Jing Xiang hated them and told Taizu, “The new dynasty needs upright men; the Xuns are without conduct and cannot stand in court.

sentences.zh: 」於是父子皆勒歸田里，乃依朱友謙於河中。

translations.literal: Thereupon father and son were both forced back to their villages and relied on Zhu Youqian at Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Both were forced home and relied on Zhu Youqian at Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 其後，友謙叛梁降晉，晉王將即帝位，求唐故臣在者，以備百官之闕，友謙遣循至魏州。

translations.literal: Later Youqian rebelled against Liang and submitted to Jin; the Prince of Jin was about to take the throne and sought Tang old ministers still alive to fill the gaps in the hundred offices; Youqian sent Xun to Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later Youqian rebelled to Jin; the Prince of Jin sought Tang ministers to fill office; Youqian sent Xun to Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 是時梁未滅，晉諸將相多不欲晉王即位。

translations.literal: At that time Liang was not yet destroyed; many of Jin’s generals and chiefs did not wish the Prince of Jin to take the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was not yet destroyed; many Jin generals did not want the Prince of Jin to enthrone himself.

sentences.zh: 晉王之意雖銳，將相大臣未有贊成其議者。

translations.literal: Though the Prince of Jin’s will was keen, among generals and great ministers none yet approved the plan.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin was eager, but his generals and ministers had not yet approved.

sentences.zh: 循始至魏州，望州廨聽事即拜，謂之「拜殿」。

translations.literal: When Xun first reached Weizhou, seeing the prefectural offices’ audience hall he bowed at once—called “bowing to the hall.”
translations.idiomatic: When Xun reached Weizhou he saw the audience hall and bowed at once—the “hall bow.”

sentences.zh: 及入謁，蹈舞呼萬歲而稱臣，晉王大悅。

translations.literal: On entering audience he danced, shouted “Long live,” and styled himself minister; the Prince of Jin was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: In audience he danced, shouted “Long live,” and styled himself minister; the Prince of Jin was delighted.

sentences.zh: 明日又獻「畫日筆」三十管，晉王益喜，因以循為節度副使。

translations.literal: The next day he also presented thirty “day-marking brushes”; the Prince of Jin was still more pleased and made Xun deputy military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Next day he presented thirty “day-marking brushes”; the Prince of Jin made him deputy military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 已而病卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 莊宗即位，贈左僕射。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne, Xun was posthumously made Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong took the throne, Xun was posthumously made Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 楷，同光中為尚書員外郎。

translations.literal: Kai in the Tongguang era was Vice Director in the Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Kai in the Tongguang era was a vice director in the Ministry.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，大臣欲理其駁謚之罪，以憂死。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, great ministers wished to punish his crime of disputing the posthumous title; he died of anxiety.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong took the throne, ministers wished to punish his posthumous-title crime; he died of anxiety.

sentences.zh: 當唐之亡也，又有杜曉者，字明遠。

translations.literal: When Tang was perishing there was also Du Xiao, courtesy name Mingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang fell there was also Du Xiao, courtesy name Mingyuan.

sentences.zh: 祖審權，父讓能，皆為唐相。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shenquan and father Rangneng were both Tang chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shenquan and father Rangneng were both Tang chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 昭宗時，王行瑜、李茂貞兵犯京師，昭宗殺讓能於臨臯以自解。

translations.literal: Under Zhaozong, Wang Xingyu and Li Maozhen’s armies attacked the capital; Zhaozong killed Rangneng at Linhao to excuse himself.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhaozong, Wang Xingyu and Li Maozhen attacked the capital; Zhaozong killed Rangneng at Linhao to excuse himself.

sentences.zh: 曉以父死無罪，居喪哀毀；

translations.literal: Xiao, holding that his father died without crime, mourned in destruction of his person;
translations.idiomatic: Xiao held his father innocent and mourned until he was broken;

sentences.zh: 服除，布衣幅巾，自廢十餘年。

translations.literal: when mourning ended he wore plain cloth and headcloth and kept himself idle more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: when mourning ended he wore plain cloth and kept idle more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 崔胤判鹽鐵，辟巡官，除畿縣尉，直昭文館，皆不起。

translations.literal: Cui Yin as salt-iron commissioner took him as touring officer, made him metropolitan district captain, and attached him to the Zhaowen Hall—all he would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yin as salt-iron commissioner, metropolitan posts, and Zhaowen Hall attachment—all he refused.

sentences.zh: 崔遠判戶部，又辟巡官，或謂曉曰：「嵇康死，子紹自廢不出仕，山濤以物理責之，乃仕。

translations.literal: Cui Yuan as revenue commissioner again took him as touring officer; someone said to Xiao: “When Ji Kang died, his son Shao kept himself idle and would not serve; Shan Tao rebuked him on natural principle and only then did he serve.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuan as revenue commissioner took him again; someone told Xiao, “When Ji Kang died, his son Shao would not serve until Shan Tao rebuked him on principle.

sentences.zh: 吾子忍令杜氏歲時鋪席祭其先人同匹庶乎？

translations.literal: Can you bear to let the Du clan at the seasons spread mats and sacrifice to their forebears like commoners?”
translations.idiomatic: Can you bear to let the Du clan sacrifice to their forebears like commoners?”

sentences.zh: 」曉乃為之起。

translations.literal: Xiao then took office for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao then took office.

sentences.zh: 累遷膳部郎中、翰林學士。

translations.literal: He rose step by step to Director of the Board of Food and Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Director of the Board of Food and Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 梁太祖即位，遷工部侍郎奉旨。

translations.literal: When Taizu of Liang took the throne, Xiao was moved to Vice Minister of Works with imperial commission.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang’s Taizu took the throne, Xiao became Vice Minister of Works with imperial commission.

sentences.zh: 開平二年，拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiping he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Concurrent Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiping’s second year he became Vice Director and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 友珪立，遷禮部尚書、集賢殿大學士。

translations.literal: When Yougui took the throne, Xiao was moved to Minister of Rites and Grand Academician of the Hall for Assembling the Worthy.
translations.idiomatic: When Yougui took the throne, Xiao became Minister of Rites and Grand Academician of the Hall for Assembling the Worthy.

sentences.zh: 袁象先等討賊，兵大掠，曉為亂兵所殺，贈右僕射。

translations.literal: When Yuan Xiangxian and others punished the traitor, the army looted greatly; Xiao was killed by mutinous soldiers and posthumously made Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Xiangxian punished the traitor, the army looted; Xiao was killed by mutineers and posthumously made Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 始為朋黨之論者誰歟？

translations.literal: Who first made the theory of factions?
translations.idiomatic: Who first made the theory of factions?

sentences.zh: 甚乎作俑者也，真可謂不仁之人哉！

translations.literal: How extreme—the one who first made the mold! Men who may truly be called without benevolence!
translations.idiomatic: How extreme—the one who made the mold! Truly men without benevolence!

sentences.zh: 予嘗至繁城，讀《魏受禪碑》，見漢之群臣稱魏功德，而大書深刻，自列其姓名，以誇耀於世。

translations.literal: I once went to Fancheng and read the “Stele of Wei’s Reception of the Abdication,” and saw Han’s ministers praising Wei’s merit, carving deep and large, listing their own names to boast to the world.
translations.idiomatic: I once read at Fancheng the “Stele of Wei’s Reception of the Abdication”—Han ministers praising Wei’s merit, names carved deep to boast to the world.

sentences.zh: 又讀《梁實錄》，見文蔚等所為如此，未嘗不為之流涕也。

translations.literal: I also read the “Veritable Records of Liang” and saw Wenwei and the rest acting thus—I have never failed to weep over it.
translations.idiomatic: I also read Liang’s Veritable Records and saw Wenwei and the rest—never without tears.

sentences.zh: 夫以國予人而自誇耀，及遂相之，此非小人，孰能為也？

translations.literal: To give the state to another and boast of it, and then become his chancellor—if not petty men, who could do this?
translations.idiomatic: To hand over the state and boast, then serve as chancellor—if not petty men, who could do this?

sentences.zh: 漢、唐之末，舉其朝皆小人也，而其君子者何在哉！

translations.literal: At the ends of Han and Tang, raise their courts—all petty men; where then were the gentlemen?
translations.idiomatic: At the ends of Han and Tang, their courts were all petty men—where were the gentlemen?

sentences.zh: 當漢之亡也，先以朋黨禁錮天下賢人君子，而立其朝者，皆小人也，然後漢從而亡。

translations.literal: When Han was perishing, it first used factions to imprison the realm’s worthy gentlemen and upright men, and those who stood in its court were all petty men—then Han followed into extinction.
translations.idiomatic: Han first imprisoned worthy gentlemen as factions, filled court with petty men—then Han fell.

sentences.zh: 及唐之亡也，又先以朋黨盡殺朝廷之士，而其餘存者，皆庸懦不肖傾險之人也，然後唐從而亡。

translations.literal: When Tang was perishing, it again first used factions to kill all court scholars, and those who remained were mediocre, cowardly, unworthy, treacherous men—then Tang followed into extinction.
translations.idiomatic: Tang again killed court scholars as factions; what remained were cowards and traitors—then Tang fell.

sentences.zh: 夫欲空人之國而去其君子者，必進朋黨之說；

translations.literal: Those who wish to empty a man’s state and remove its gentlemen must advance the theory of factions;
translations.idiomatic: To empty a state and remove its gentlemen, advance faction theory;

sentences.zh: 欲孤人主之勢而蔽其耳目者，必進朋黨之說；

translations.literal: those who wish to isolate the sovereign’s power and block his eyes and ears must advance the theory of factions;
translations.idiomatic: to isolate the sovereign and block his ears, advance faction theory;

sentences.zh: 欲奪國而與人者，必進朋黨之說。

translations.literal: those who wish to seize the state and give it to another must advance the theory of factions.
translations.idiomatic: to seize the state and give it away, advance faction theory.

sentences.zh: 夫為君子者，故嘗寡過，小人欲加之罪，則有可誣者，有不可誣者，不能遍及也。

translations.literal: Gentlemen by nature seldom err; petty men wishing to attach guilt to them have what can be slandered and what cannot— they cannot reach everyone.
translations.idiomatic: Gentlemen seldom err; petty men slandering them can reach some, not all.

sentences.zh: 至欲舉天下之善，求其類而盡去之，惟指以為朋黨耳。

translations.literal: But to raise all the good under Heaven, seek their kind, and remove them entirely—only point and call them factions.
translations.idiomatic: To remove all good under Heaven, call every kindred gathering a faction.

sentences.zh: 故其親戚故舊，謂之朋黨可也；

translations.literal: Thus kin and old associates may be called factions;
translations.idiomatic: Kin and old associates—factions;

sentences.zh: 交遊執友，謂之朋黨可也；

translations.literal: friends and sworn companions may be called factions;
translations.idiomatic: friends and sworn companions—factions;

sentences.zh: 宦學相同，謂之朋黨可也；

translations.literal: those of the same official schooling may be called factions;
translations.idiomatic: the same schooling—factions;

sentences.zh: 門生故吏，謂之朋黨可也。

translations.literal: students and old subordinates may be called factions.
translations.idiomatic: students and old subordinates—factions.

sentences.zh: 是數者，皆其類也，皆善人也。

translations.literal: These several are all their kind—all good men.
translations.idiomatic: All their kind—all good men.

sentences.zh: 故曰：欲空人之國而去其君子者，惟以朋黨罪之，則無免者矣。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: wishing to empty a man’s state and remove its gentlemen, charge them as factions and none escape.
translations.idiomatic: Charge gentlemen as factions and none escape—the state is emptied.

sentences.zh: 夫善善之相樂，以其類同，此自然之理也。

translations.literal: Good men delighting in good is because their kind is the same—this is nature’s principle.
translations.idiomatic: Good men delight in good because their kind is the same—nature’s law.

sentences.zh: 故聞善者必相稱譽，稱譽則謂之朋黨，得善者必相薦引，薦引則謂之朋黨，使人聞善不敢稱譽，人主之耳不聞有善於下矣，見善不敢薦引，則人主之目不得見善人矣。

translations.literal: Thus those who hear good must praise one another—praise is called faction; those who gain good must recommend one another—recommendation is called faction; making men hear good yet dare not praise leaves the sovereign’s ears without good below; seeing good yet daring not recommend leaves the sovereign’s eyes without good men.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing good, men praise—praise is faction; gaining good, men recommend—recommendation is faction; forbid praise and the sovereign’s ears hear no good; forbid recommendation and his eyes see no good men.

sentences.zh: 善人日遠，而小人日進，則為人主者，倀倀然誰與之圖治安之計哉？

translations.literal: Good men daily farther, petty men daily nearer—then for the one who is sovereign, who is there to plan with him for order and peace?
translations.idiomatic: Good men recede, petty men advance—who then plans order and peace with the sovereign?

sentences.zh: 故曰：欲孤人主之勢而蔽其耳目者，必用朋黨之說也。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: wishing to isolate the sovereign’s power and block his eyes and ears, one must use the theory of factions.
translations.idiomatic: To isolate the sovereign and block his ears, use faction theory.

sentences.zh: 一君子存，群小人雖眾，必有所忌，而有所不敢為，惟空國而無君子，然後小人得肆誌於無所不為，則漢魏、唐梁之際是也。

translations.literal: While one gentleman remains, though petty men are many they must have something they fear and dare not do—only when the state is empty of gentlemen do petty men then freely set their will with nothing they dare not do—such were the times of Han-Wei, Tang-Liang.
translations.idiomatic: One gentleman left, petty men still fear; empty the state of gentlemen and petty men do as they please—Han-Wei, Tang-Liang.

sentences.zh: 故曰：可奪國而予人者，由其國無君子，空國而無君子，由以朋黨而去之也。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: one can seize the state and give it to another because his state has no gentlemen; empty a state of gentlemen by removing them as factions.
translations.idiomatic: States are given away because no gentlemen remain; gentlemen are removed by calling them factions.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，朋黨之說，人主可不察哉！

translations.literal: Alas—the theory of factions: can a sovereign fail to examine it!
translations.idiomatic: Alas—faction theory: can a sovereign fail to examine it!

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰「一言可以喪邦」者，其是之謂與！

translations.literal: The “Records” says “one word can lose a state”—is this not what is meant!
translations.idiomatic: The Records say “one word can lose a state”—is this not it!

sentences.zh: 可不鑒哉！

translations.literal: Can one fail to take it as a mirror!
translations.idiomatic: Take it as a mirror!

sentences.zh: 可不戒哉！

translations.literal: Can one fail to guard against it!
translations.idiomatic: Guard against it!
